questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. 

There is ____ a lot to learn from nature.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Quite.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Quite** is an **adverb** used to describe when something is a **little or a lot.**__
 
• **Quite a lot **is a phrase or an idiom that means **a large number or a considerable amount.**
 __
 
• **Example: ***Certain jobs involve**** quite a lot ****of travel.*
 
 
 
• *​*Here, in this sentence, **quite a lot **infers that we can learn many things from nature.
 
• The most appropriate word to fill in the given blank is** quite.**
 
• This makes **option 3** the correct answer. 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__** 

 
• **Quiet **and** quite** are examples of **homophones.**
 
• **Homophones** are words where each of two or more words have the same pronunciation but different meanings, origins, or spelling.
 
• **Quiet** is an** adjective** used to describe something or someone who is reticent or silent.
 
• **Quite** is an **adverb** used to describe when something is a little or a lot but not completely.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

________ we gave them was some homemade ice cream.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**What**'.

__
 
• The word "**What**" correctly introduces the noun clause that serves as the subject of the sentence.
 
• This construction conveys that the thing given to "them" was homemade ice cream.
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and 3 do not fit this context and are grammatically incorrect here.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"What we gave them was some homemade ice cream."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "Which"** is incorrect because it typically introduces a relative clause, not a noun clause.
 
• **Option 2: "When"** is incorrect because it refers to time, which is not relevant in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "While"** is incorrect because it indicates a period of time, which also doesn't fit the context.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

David always takes extra effort and ________ the assignments on time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "submits."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Subject-verb agreement is a fundamental grammatical principle that dictates that the form of the verb should match the number of the subject.
 
• Since **"David"** is a singular noun, the corresponding verb should also be in the singular form, which is** "submits."**

 
 
• The grammatical reason to write the word **"submits"** in the blank is to maintain subject-verb agreement and ensure that the sentence is syntactically correct.
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

 

**Correct sentence**: *David always takes extra effort and **submits**__ the assignments on time.*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.**

He was ______ in a pool of blood near a neighbour's house.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Lying**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Lying**" is the correct choice in this context. It's the present participle form of the verb "lie," which means to recline or be in a horizontal position.
 
• In the sentence, it describes the person's state of being found in a pool of blood, which is a horizontal position.
 
• We are describing the person's physical position at a particular point in the past.
 
• The person was found in a pool of blood, and "lying" accurately conveys this position.

Therefore, the correct answer is** option 3**.

**Complete sentence**: *He was lying __in a pool of blood near a neighbour's house.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "**Lain**" is the past participle of the verb "lie," but it's used in the perfect tenses, like "has lain" or "had lain." It's not suitable for the simple past tense in this sentence.
 
• "**Laying**" is the present participle of the verb "lay," which is transitive and requires an object. It doesn't work in this sentence because there's no object after it.
 
• "**Lied**" is the past tense of the verb "lie," but it's used when someone intentionally tells a falsehood. It doesn't fit the context of the sentence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

Chris and I play tennis together regularly, but ________ of us can play very well.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4) i.e. neither.**

 
• The sentence uses 'but' which means that the speaker introduces a contradictory statement after 'but'.
 
• We can reject options 1 and 2 as they would give the sentence positive meanings. 
 
• None is used when there are multiple options and not even one is true, hence option 3 is also rejected.
 
• **Neither is used when there are two options and not even one is true. **It means 'not the one nor the other of two people or things; not either.'
 
• Here, we have two people. Hence, we will use **'neither'**.
 
• So, only option 4 is correct.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

These dates are from Dubai, __isn't it__?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**aren't they**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This sentence is an example of a **tag question**.
 
• Question tags are always placed at the end.
 
• A **positive **statement is followed by a **negative** question** **tag.
 
• A **negative **statement is followed by a **positive **question tag.
 
• The auxiliary verb used in the question tag is according to the statement.
 
• In the given sentence, the correct form of the question tag should be "aren't they" as the **subject**(dates) is **plural.**

**Hence, the correct sentence is**__: These dates are from Dubai, *__**aren't they**__*?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Contractions are words formed by shortening the words by omitting some letters.
 
• Words like **isn't it, aren't they, could've, and would've** are also known as **contractions**.
 
• Isn't: It is contracted form of "is not"; aren't: are not.
 
• If the subject is **singular**, we use the contraction **isn't it?**
 
• Question tags are always separated from the statement by a **comma**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.**

As you make your way __in the interior of__ Red Fort, lush green gardens greet you.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1), i.e., Into the interior of.**

**Explanation**:

**Let's look at how the given prepositions are used:**

**In**- showing movement where something becomes surrounded by something else.*** Example: I am living in London.***

**Into**- expressing movement where something is physically enclosed by something else. ***Example: I put the glass into the fridge.***

**On**- physically in contact with and supported by (a surface). ***Example: The apple is on the table.***

**Along**- moving in a constant direction with another entity, such as a path, river etc.*** Example: We were moving along the banks of Ganga.***

**Important Point:**

The sentence uses the preposition '**in**', which is incorrect here.

__The sentence talks about '**the interior**' of the Red Fort. So, the preposition must also reflect this physical enclosing of one object by another.__

Given the context, only the preposition '**Into**' is appropriate here.

**Confusion Point:**

The preposition '**along**' may seem correct; but it is not. '**Along**' needs another fixed path with a direction, with which a person/thing moves. 'Interior' is the general inside area; it does not suggest a specific direction.

**Thus, the rectified sentence is:** *As you make your way __**into the interior of**__ Red Fort, lush green gardens greet you.*

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The sentence describes a sequence of events, with the old man walking through the forest and then hearing someone crying for help. • "When" is a conjunction that is used to indicate a specific point in time or a cause-and-effect relationship between two events.(जब) • Example: I was in the office when it happened. • In this case,** "when" is the most appropriate option because it connects the old man's actions with the sound of someone crying for help.** • Thus, the correct sentence will be: • One day, an old man was walking through the forest when__ suddenly he heard someone crying for help. Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** • Option 1 (which) is a relative pronoun that is used to introduce a subordinate clause that provides additional information about a noun or pronoun in the main clause. (कौन सा) • Option 3 (while) is a conjunction that is used to indicate that two actions are happening at the same time, but in this case, the actions are not happening simultaneously.(जबकि) • Option 4 (than) is a conjunction that is used to compare two things, but it does not fit the context of the sentence.(की अपेक्षा) 42:T8cb,
